papers.title: Deterministic regularisation of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic. This resolves an important open problem in the complexity of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem. Given a complex contraction $A$ of order $n\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, we compute a perturbation $E$ with $\|E\|<\delta$ such that $A+E$ has simple spectrum. The ratio of its eigenbasis condition number to its minimum eigenvalue gap is at most $C(n/\delta)^{20/3}$. The algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of $A+E$. It uses $O(n^3\log^d(n/\delta))$ real-field operations and comparisons, where $C$ and $d$ are absolute constants. We choose the rank-one perturbations using a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus. A quadratic penalty controls how far the accumulated updates move the matrix. By using the same reference eigenbasis for several updates, we can estimate all the current projector norms while recovering only the directions needed for the next perturbation.

papers.title: Gaussian Belief Propagation and Periodic Jacobi Matrices on Trees: Spectral Curve, Antibound Poles, and Fixed Points
papers.abstract: Diagonal Green functions of a periodic Jacobi operator on a universal covering tree satisfy the scalar Gaussian belief propagation covariance equations on the finite connected loopless base multigraph. At cycle rank at least two, the Green functions continue to simple antibound poles at both Perron values for arbitrary real potentials and nonzero real weights. This proves the conjecture of Christiansen, Simon and Zinchenko. For positive weights the pole result includes self-loops. On loopless graphs the lower pole is the walk-summability threshold. Each energy strictly between it and the spectral bottom has at least two fixed points with positive definite local beliefs. On a connected simple graph, some coefficients yield a compact component of positive solutions exactly when the graph contains two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. The covariance curve is generically irreducible, with one sheet per edge subset with no vertex of degree one. For cycle rank at least two and generic real coefficients, the diagonal Green functions, infinite half-tree $m$-functions and the density-of-states Stieltjes transform all have this degree, answering a question of Avni, Breuer and Simon. Then all eigenvalues of the signed Jacobi matrices are antibound poles. Signed principal submatrices classify finite points with nonzero residue of $(\sum_i V_i) dz$, where $V_i$ are the vertex variances. We give a genus formula. Near zero potentials and unit weights on $K_4$, independently varying the coefficients leaves the cover spectrum an interval. This refutes Avni, Breuer and Simon's conjecture on the density of parameters with all gaps open. In block models, generic irreducibility and a uniqueness criterion extend, and at uniform dimension $p$ the degree can exceed $L^p$ for scalar degree $L$. Part of the scalar theory is formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar H\"older domains
papers.abstract: We prove strict hot spots and the absence of interior critical points for every nonzero real eigenfunction at the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of a bounded simply connected planar H\"older domain. The H\"older hypothesis is the quasihyperbolic boundary condition; equivalently, the derivative of a Riemann map belongs to $L^p$ for some $p>2$. The eigenvalue may be multiple, and the boundary need not be Jordan; boundary extrema are then interpreted through the continuous conformal pullback. The theorem includes bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains, polygonal Jordan domains with reentrant corners, bounded convex domains, simply connected John domains, and quasidisks. We extend the reciprocal Green kernel method for smooth domains by constructing boundary primitives for the transformed Neumann gradient and proving a multiplier estimate uniform under conformal exhaustion. Approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace handles splitting of a multiple eigenvalue.

papers.title: Space-time almost periodicity for the defocusing NLS hierarchy via local Toeplitz operators
papers.abstract: We study the defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger hierarchy for reflectionless initial data with Dirac spectrum $E$. Under a gap moment condition of order $m$ and the assumption that $E$ is homogeneous, we prove existence and space-time almost periodicity of a global classical solution through order $m$ for every such initial datum. More generally, it suffices that $\mathbb C\setminus E$ be a Dirichlet regular Widom domain satisfying the direct Cauchy theorem and that the gap maxima of a weighted Green potential be summable, in addition to the gap moment condition. We obtain the frequencies by summing the upper and lower boundary values of the corrected powers $z^r$ on each gap and use local Toeplitz operators to reconstruct the potential from the gap phases. We also prove uniqueness under bounds on the spatial derivatives.

papers.title: The first Fu\v{c}\'ik curve of the $p$-Laplacian on compact quantum graphs: slopes at the diagonal and nonresonance
papers.abstract: We study the Fu\v{c}\'{\i}k spectrum of the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<\infty$, on a compact connected quantum graph, with Dirichlet conditions on a possibly empty set $V_D$ of vertices whose removal does not disconnect the graph and Kirchhoff conditions at the others. We construct the first nontrivial curve $\mathfrak C$ of the spectrum by a mountain pass argument and show that it is Lipschitz and strictly decreasing. As the parameter tends to infinity, $\mathfrak C$ tends to the first eigenvalue if $V_D\neq\emptyset$, and otherwise to the smallest first eigenvalue obtained by a Dirichlet condition at a single point. If the second eigenvalue is simple, we compute the two one-sided slopes of $\mathfrak C$ at the diagonal. The curve is differentiable there if and only if the positive and negative parts of the second eigenfunction have the same $L^p$ norm. On three-edge stars these norms differ for suitable edge lengths and every $p$, so the Lipschitz regularity is optimal. For $p=2$ the simplicity assumption can be dropped, and for a simple eigenvalue the corner is the crossing of the two smooth branches of the spectrum through the diagonal point. Finally, we prove a nonresonance result in which, for $V_D=\emptyset$, the ratio $f(x,s)/|s|^{p-2}s$ may be arbitrarily large at $+\infty$, provided it stays below the threshold at $-\infty$.

papers.title: A simple counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for excited states
papers.abstract: For an even number of non-interacting fermions on the one-dimensional unit torus, a semi-explicit counterexample to the Hohenberg--Kohn theorem for excited states is exhibited. Indeed, for each $n = 2l$, it is shown that there exist constants $m \in (0, 1)$ and $\ell > 0$ such that an $n$-body system with the rescaled Lam\'e potential $v_*(x) = 2m \ell^2 \operatorname{sn}^2(\ell x; m)$ has a simple first excited energy and a first excited-state particle density which is constant on the torus. By translating this potential, we exhibit a non-trivial one-parameter family of potentials, all of which have a constant first excited-state density. As such, the potential-to-density map is not one-to-one in this setting. Under a spectral nonresonance assumption, we obtain the same nonuniqueness at a simple excited energy for odd $n \geq 3$. We also explore connections to the classification problem of elastica in the plane when $n = 2$, and outline some related questions of interest.

papers.title: Rayleigh's conjecture for clamped plates in dimensions four and five
papers.abstract: In 1877, Lord Rayleigh conjectured that the disk minimizes the fundamental frequency of a clamped plate of prescribed area. We prove the higher-dimensional conjecture in dimensions four and five by establishing a sharp comparison between the first clamped-plate eigenvalue and the square of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue on the same domain. The proof uses a nonlinear transformation built from the ball eigenfunctions. A local identity keeps all terms of the Hessian. Exact coefficient inequalities and bounds for the infinite remainders establish positivity, while a weak formulation handles sign changes and critical sets. We characterize equality in the volume inequality and identify an obstruction to this transformation in dimension six.

papers.title: A strict Neumann-Dirichlet eigenvalue inequality on planar domains
papers.abstract: On simply connected, bounded planar Lipschitz domains it is known from our earlier work that the ($k+2$)-nd eigenvalue of the Neumann Laplacian cannot exceed the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. In this note we sharpen this statement by showing that this inequality is always strict. This was previously only known under additional assumptions.

papers.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
papers.abstract: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.

papers.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
papers.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g \lambda_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8\pi^2/\sqrt{3} + 8\pi$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

papers.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
papers.abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schr\"odinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Gol\'enia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.

papers.title: Infinitely many spectral gaps for Anderson--Bernoulli operators with sparse periodic backgrounds
papers.abstract: We consider discrete Anderson--Bernoulli operators with a periodic background. At a single coupling, every minimal period of at least three admits a background with at most four nonzero sites per period whose almost sure spectrum has infinitely many gaps. We give two constructions. The first uses at most seven nonzero sites per period and fixes the accumulation point at zero. For periods of at least five, the second uses exactly four nonzero sites per period and takes the lowest Dirichlet eigenvalue of the inserted chain as the accumulation point. In both constructions the gaps approach from the right. The widths of the selected gaps and their distances to the accumulation point are comparable to a common geometric factor divided by the period in the first family and by its cube in the second. Spectral intervals of comparable length separate successive gaps in each selected sequence.

papers.title: Quantum Variance of Holomorphic Modular Forms and Benjamini-Schramm Convergence
papers.abstract: We study quantum variance for holomorphic modular forms of fixed weight on sequences of compact hyperbolic surfaces converging to the hyperbolic plane in the sense of Benjamini-Schramm. We first show that quantum ergodicity need not hold for an arbitrary choice of orthonormal basis, even for sequences with a uniform lower bound on the injectivity radius and a uniform spectral gap. The counterexample is constructed using a tower of coverings and arises from the identity contribution in the automorphic kernel. We then show that this obstruction is exceptional from the point of view of the choice of basis. For a Haar random orthonormal basis of holomorphic modular forms, the quantum variance converges to zero with probability tending to one uniformly over all observables with bounded supremum norm. The proof combines estimates for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a projected multiplication operator with the Haar expectation of the quantum variance, concentration of measure on the special unitary group and a finite-dimensional approximation of the space of observables.

papers.title: On the Spectrum of the Iwatsuka Hamiltonian with Equal Magnetic Field Limits
papers.abstract: We consider the two-dimensional magnetic Laplacian associated with a magnetic field that depends on a single spatial variable, known as the Iwatsuka Hamiltonian. We focus on the equal-limit case, where the magnetic field is of the form $b(\cdot)=b_\infty+q(\cdot)$, with $b_\infty>0$ and $q\in C_0(\mathbb R)$. We prove that the Iwatsuka Hamiltonian admits an absolutely continuous spectrum whenever $q$ is compactly supported and has a constant sign near one edge of its support.

papers.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
papers.abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

papers.title: Global Flows for the KdV Hierarchy with Initial Conditions Having No Restriction on Schr\"odinger Spectra
papers.abstract: When one of the authors constructed the KdV flow for a broad class of initial data, he imposed a restriction that the underlying Schr\"odinger operators with the initial data as potentials were bounded from below. We remove this restriction and establish the flow on a space of initial data that are bounded from above and possibly unbounded from below.

papers.title: Asymptotics for Riesz means of integrable polygons
papers.abstract: We prove complete asymptotic expansions for Riesz means of order $\gamma > 0$ for the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on integrable polygons. The coefficients of the first three terms are the familiar ones involving the area, perimeter, and corner angles of the polygon. The coefficients of the lower-order terms are given by convergent trigonometric series. The proof is based on heat trace identities for integrable polygons, together with large-argument asymptotics for Bessel functions.

papers.title: Eigenvector geometry and spectra of doubly stochastic matrices
papers.abstract: Let $U_N$ be the union of the convex hulls of the $k$th roots of unity for $1\le k\le N$. We prove that, for $N\ge10^{213}$, every convex combination of two permutation matrices of order $N$ has spectrum in $U_N$. The ordered pairs of columns selected in the rows form directed cycles. The proof uses the winding about the origin and the Fourier coefficients of the eigenvector coordinates along one cycle. For arbitrary doubly stochastic matrices, we form a polygon by assigning distinct columns to selected eigenvector coordinates. Near a root of unity of exact order $q\le N$, the full eigenvalue region agrees locally with the regular $q\lfloor N/q\rfloor$-gon. For $N\ge256$, suppose an eigenvalue lies outside $U_N$. In every associated eigenvector $v$ normalised by $\max_i|v_i|=1$, some coordinate $v_j$ lies strictly inside the convex hull of the coordinates and satisfies $|v_j|^2>1-100/N$.

papers.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $\Gamma$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $\Gamma$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $\Gamma$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.

papers.title: Spectral Dehn Functions: Hyperbolicity, Filling Geometry and Diffusion
papers.abstract: We show that Dirichlet eigenvalues of van Kampen diagrams can distinguish groups whose Dehn functions have the same order. The Dehn function bounds the least filling area in terms of word length. We use the random walk on the faces, stopped at the exterior. For each null word we take the infimum, over its fillings, of the reciprocal of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, then maximize over words of length at most $n$. We call this the spectral Dehn function. Its coarse growth is a quasi-isometry invariant for presentations whose generators form a word ball and whose relators are all null words of length at most three. In such a presentation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the boundary word of a square can have a filling with more faces and a larger first eigenvalue than any of its least-area fillings. For two groups with quartic Dehn functions, it is at most $Cn^4$ for one and at least $cn^6/(\log n)^2$ for the other. The spectral Dehn function is bounded exactly for word-hyperbolic groups. For other finitely presented groups it grows at least as fast as $n^2/(\log n)^2$. In these presentations the bound is sharp for non-hyperbolic automatic groups and for non-hyperbolic groups acting properly and cocompactly by isometries on proper geodesic Lipschitz $1$-connected spaces. For the face walk we maximize the expected absorption time over starting faces. In these classes its supremum over least-area fillings of cyclically reduced null words of length at most $n$ has order $n^2$. Taking the infimum over all fillings of each null word before maximizing over words of length at most $n$ gives order $n^2/\log n$ in these presentations. Under a quadratic isoperimetric inequality, every non-hyperbolic group has, for each sufficiently large $n$, a null word of length at most $n$ whose least-area fillings have, for the face and vertex walks, $j$th Dirichlet eigenvalue of order $j/n^2$ for $1\le j\le cn^2$.
